compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: RTX5090M: 896 GB/s BW, 82 SMs. 67M fp16 elements per tensor = 134MB read + 134MB write = ~402MB traffic. Min latency ~0.45ms at peak BW.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Pure elementwise add: 1 FLOP per 6 bytes touched. Compute negligible; purely BW-bound.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Compute cores will be idle; nothing to gain from tensor cores.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Need to saturate 896 GB/s. Wide vectorized loads (uint4 = 8 fp16 per lane) crucial. Avoid scalar Buffer<float16_t> loads which may be inefficient.
memory_bandwidth.risk: If we use scalar fp16 loads, we may get <50% of peak BW. Need ByteAddressBuffer or wider types.

register_pressure.notes: Trivial — only a few regs needed for vectorized add. Plenty of headroom for unrolling.

nodes.notes:
ANALYSIS:
1) CLASSIFY: Pure elementwise binary add. No reductions, dense contiguous access, fp16. 67,108,864 elements total (16*2048*2048). Flatten to 1D.
2) MATH: out[i] = x[i] + y[i], fully independent across i.
3) LAYOUT: All three tensors contiguous fp16, identical shape. Read-once, write-once, no reuse. Stream-through pattern.
4) REGIMES: (a) BW-bound large N — current case, dominant; (b) Latency-bound small N — N/A here; (c) Issue-bound if too few threads — avoid by launching ~1M+ threads.
5) KNOBS: vectorization width (1/2/4/8 fp16 per thread), threads/group (64-256), elements per thread (loop unroll), buffer type (typed Buffer<float16_t> vs ByteAddressBuffer with uint2/uint4 + bitcast), dispatch shape (1D vs 3D).
6) SKELETON: 1D dispatch; each thread loads K consecutive fp16 from x and y via wide load, adds, stores K fp16 to out. No shared memory, no sync.
7) FAMILIES: (A) Wide vectorized ByteAddressBuffer (load uint4 = 8 fp16, bitcast, add, store) — best BW efficiency; (B) Typed Buffer<float16_t> with 1 elem/thread — simplest, may underperform on BW; (C) Typed Buffer<float16_t> with 4-8 elems/thread unroll — middle ground.
FULL FUSION: trivially fused already (single op).
PRIMARY LIMITER: DRAM bandwidth. Target ~0.45-0.6 ms.
DISPATCH MATH: 67108864 elems / 8 elems-per-thread = 8388608 threads / 256 threads-per-group = 32768 groups. Fits in single dim < 65535? No — use multi-dim or larger groups. With 8 elems/thread and 256 tpg → groups=32768, need [32768,1,1] or split.

action.description: Use ByteAddressBuffer for x, y and RWByteAddressBuffer for out. Each thread loads uint4 (16 bytes = 8 fp16) from each input, bitcasts to two min16float4 (or unpacks via f16tof32), performs vector add, stores uint4. Use 256 threads/group, 8 elems/thread → 2048 elems/group → 32768 groups in X (fits in 65535 limit).
action.rationale: Wide loads are essential to saturate 896 GB/s on a pure-BW kernel. uint4 transactions coalesce well and minimize instruction count.
action.title: Wide vectorized ByteAddressBuffer (uint4, 8 fp16/thread)

kernel_summary: Pure elementwise fp16 add of two (16,2048,2048) tensors — 67.1M independent operations, fully bandwidth-bound on the RTX5090M's 896 GB/s GDDR7. Total traffic ~402 MB (2 reads + 1 write of 134 MB each), giving a BW-limited floor near 0.45 ms. No reductions, no reuse, no compute pressure: success hinges entirely on issuing the widest coalesced memory transactions possible (preferably 128-bit uint4 via ByteAddressBuffer), giving each thread enough work (8-16 fp16) to amortize address math, and launching enough threads (~1M+) across 82 SMs to hide DRAM latency. Constraints: cs_6_8 with 16-bit types, dispatch group counts ≤65535 per dim, no CBVs/root constants available so shape is hardcoded.
open_questions: Does the cs_6_8 compiler/driver issue true 128-bit loads for Buffer<float16_t4>, or must we use ByteAddressBuffer + uint4 + bitcast to guarantee it?
What is the optimal elements-per-thread (4 vs 8 vs 16 vs 32) to balance MLP and instruction overhead on Blackwell?
Is the dispatch limit per-dim 65535 — do we need to split into [gx, gy, 1] for >65535 groups?
Will using min16float4 add be lowered to native fp16 vector adds, or promoted to fp32 (still fine for BW but more regs)?
Is there any benefit to using groupshared as a staging buffer, or is it pure overhead for this streaming pattern? (Almost certainly overhead.)
Should output be written via RWByteAddressBuffer.Store4 (uint4) for symmetry with reads, and does this fully coalesce?
How does the evaluator validate numerics — does fp32 intermediate accumulation matter for rtol=0.01 (likely not, fp16 add is exact for this tolerance)?
